Research & Engineering Lineage · BWP-L2

Evolved Workflow Management

Workflow Management represents, coordinates and enacts work across people and applications. Its central distinctions include definitions, running instances, work items and outside objects; enabling, authority and capability; and completion declaration versus achieved effect.

Current scientific findings

Workflow Management asks how definitions, running instances, work items, people and external effects can be coordinated without confusing permission, progress, completion and recipient acceptance. The current account permits loops, concurrency, local repair and adequate simple procedures.

This is the current derived account of the separately qualified scientific subject. The full scientific account and four-unit family guide provide its complete reasoning, source qualifications and detailed records. Earlier disclosure labels in the retained historical account below describe its earlier publication cutoff.

Plural genealogy and the objects being coordinated

Office information systems, document routing, transactions, cooperative work and language-action perspectives addressed different coordination problems. Formal workflow nets and pattern research sharpened control, data, resource and exception semantics. Adaptive, declarative and case-oriented work developed alternatives to fixed routing. Scientific workflow and durable execution transferred some mechanisms into settings with different reproducibility, recovery, resource and external-effect assumptions. The WfMC reference architecture consolidated terminology and interfaces; its draft of 29 November 1994 and final release of 19 January 1995 are distinct dated artefacts. None establishes a sole origin for the field. The native genealogy preserves its 20 nodes and 26 edges with the relevant type of relationship and source support. Native composition model, genealogy, source table.

The lineage’s starting distinction is among definition, running instance, work item and external object. A model is a description of possible behaviour, while a particular run has actual state and obligations. A work item may be enabled but lack an authorised, capable or available actor. A message may be sent without being received, and an engine can finish while its recipient still lacks the intended result. A usable composition therefore joins control, data, resources, interactions and observations under the conditions that actually apply. It does not treat a diagram or completion label as the whole operating world. [Ledger EWM-001 and current public-documentation intake.]

Predicates that must remain distinct

Semantics and implementation correspondence. Specified behaviour and observed implementation behaviour require a connection at the relevant engine/version/configuration. Pattern coverage or a standards badge is not sufficient. A formal model can provide a useful oracle or constraint even before an engine claim is established; the model’s inability to prove the entire receiver does not make that partial input immaterial. [Native relation R011; formal evidence cards; current report.]

Progress and acceptance. Possible completion, proper completion, deadlock freedom and inevitable termination are different claims. Real capacity, fairness or scheduling assumptions and the actual environment may matter. A successful test command can establish that a workflow ran without establishing that its scientific or business output is correct. The output oracle and receiving predicate must match the actual consumer. Loops, concurrency, streaming and interruptions remain legitimate structures; the field is not universally a DAG or serial pipeline. [Ledger EWM-011; sources on workflow soundness, Taverna and result validation.]

The accepted repair: distinct triggers, not a compulsory migration route

The substantive r2 repair responds to the adverse fidelity findings without rewriting the entire scientific programme. It retains all 77 identities and dispositions, the exact prior subject and adverse history. R021 previously made unanticipated repair an exhaustive choice between migration and external reconciliation. The corrected relation activates migration only when an existing case actually changes process semantics, and reconciliation only when an uncertain external action outcome requires it. Either, both or neither can apply. An authorised local reassignment or data correction under the same definition and without an outside effect can be a valid repair in its own right. Its permissions and consequences still matter. [Repair account, F01; model r2_scientific_repair.]

R036 now describes a compatible worklet as a conditional refinement of bounded exception repair, targeting EWM-033. A separately launched child case with compatible inputs and returned outputs need not migrate its parent. Routine late binding without an exception need not trigger that repair relation. A worklet can nevertheless fail through incompatible output, obsolete selection rules or lack of authority. The correction removes an unsupported universal endpoint; it does not prohibit a particular system from combining a worklet and a genuine migration when both actually occur. [Repair account; EWM-S036 and EWM-S037 selected passages attributed there.]

The repair also corrects the orientation of two tensions. For T002, expressiveness is favoured when a restriction would lose necessary loops, cancellation or dependencies; affordable verification is favoured when a restricted model already expresses every consequential case. For T005, adaptability is favoured when changed obligations make the old route unusable; comprehensibility and continuity can favour allowing short-lived cases to finish under old semantics when that remains acceptable. These are conditional judgements, not slogans for either side. The other eight tension records were inspected and retained. [Repair account, F02.]

Whole lineage, higher-order claims and adequate alternatives

The current model includes 63 relations, eight alternative configurations, five external interfaces, three revision boundaries, five unresolved composition obligations, ten domain models, ten tensions and 26 criticism/evolution records. These records make different arrangements inspectable rather than combining every technique into one mandatory stack. A stable small task can use a concise procedure, an accountable performer and a suitable result check. A case with long-lived or uncertain external obligations may need much stronger persistence, correlation or recovery contracts. Pure stateless recomputation, local repair, fixed handlers, old-version coexistence, supported restart and migration have distinct applicability. [Native model; current intake.]

EWM-075 is now explicitly a duplicate of EWM-003. Its closure/residual/waiver/transfer function must not be counted as a second independent closure control. EWM-076 is a conditional recovery/version configuration, not a theorem that all of its listed parents must be present in every case. The study’s composition does not establish a universally necessary product, a unique best workflow form, or empirically demonstrated benefit of its entire bundle. Source graphs, correspondence tests and finite models do not supply that missing evidence. [Ledger EWM-003, 075, 076; current novelty and duplicate judgements.]

Read the complete structured scientific records, exact source and review qualifications, and preliminary existing-owner receiving questions. Finite examples and scientific qualification establish neither deployed effectiveness nor native implementation.

BWP family and fourth-stage synthesis · Programme and state boundaries

Tradition and genealogy

The public genealogy joins office information systems and document routing, transactions, cooperative work, language-action approaches, formal workflow nets and patterns, adaptive and declarative work, case management, scientific workflows and durable execution. The WfMC reference-model draft of 29 November 1994 and final release of 19 January 1995 are distinct artefacts. That consolidation is not a claim of sole origin for the whole tradition.

Predicates and composition

A workflow definition describes behaviour; a running instance has actual state, data and outstanding obligations. A work item can be enabled without an available authorised performer. Possible completion, proper completion, deadlock freedom and inevitable termination are different claims. An engine’s completion status and a recipient’s accepted outcome are different predicates. Control, data, resources, messages and external effects must be interpreted within the actual model and environment.

The historical composition preserves concurrency, loops, interruption, recovery and revision. A small stable task can use a concise procedure, accountable performer and adequate result check. Long-lived cross-application work can require persistence, correlation, retry and version contracts. Prescribed, declarative, case-centred, scientific and replay-based forms are alternatives with distinct assumptions, not a mandatory combined stack.

Counterexamples, negatives and alternatives

A sound new definition can be invalid for a running case if a newly required step is already behind its state, a required datum has no producer or a pending callback loses its target. A timeout can leave an external effect unknown. Compensation can fail and is not universal rollback. A test-execution success can coexist with an incorrect scientific output. These are different receiving predicates, not one generic workflow PASS.

Original form

Completion is specified by final markings, explicit termination or case/stage lifecycle rules.

Problem it addressed

Parallel work, exceptions, optional/discretionary items or external actions make completion ambiguous. The consequential failure is Premature closure, abandoned work, or a successful-looking case whose required effect did not occur.

Premature closure, abandoned work, or a successful-looking case whose required effect did not occur.

Declare what instance completion establishes, what work may remain and whether residual effects are closed, transferred or explicitly accepted; do not equate terminal status with success.

Lineage class

NATIVE_WITH_SHARED_ANCESTRY_AND_DOCUMENTED_INTERSECTIONS

Original form

Cancellation regions and cancelling discriminators/partial joins alter active control-flow.

Problem it addressed

An interrupted branch can feed a later convergence point. The consequential failure is Deadlock at an AND-join or false success after bypassing unfinished required work.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Deadlock at an AND-join or false success after bypassing unfinished required work.

Mechanism

When a branch is cancelled, update join obligations according to the declared scope and activation rather than pretending that cancellation produced a success token.

Trigger or context

An interrupted branch can feed a later convergence point.

Non trigger or cheap path

Cancel the enclosing unit and restart or adjudicate it as a whole when selective continuation is unnecessary.

Dependencies or preconditions
Conditions

Join rule, cancellation scope, current branch state and a distinction between stopped control and external action.

  • EWM-034

  • EWM-036

Interpretation

Contextual semantic/evidence couplings, not a mandatory installation order or universal requirement to implement every related technique. Exact guarded relations are in COMPOSITION_MODEL.

Property application

Do not infer more than this observation; uncontrolled risk: Adding cancellation introduces analysis complexity and residual-effect obligations.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

Avoid or expose the controlled failure: Deadlock at an AND-join or false success after bypassing unfinished required work.

Evidence qualification

A mechanism-level rationale, not a measured universal benefit. Patterns and formal workflow languages specify behaviours under their stated context assumptions. Historical feature comparisons and counterexamples do not establish the best engine for a present task.

Decision or consumer

Cancellation handler, join evaluator and responsible operator.

Actor and authority boundary

Only the actor entitled to change the coordination obligation may dispense with a required branch.

Communication or interaction requirement

Signal whether the branch ceased, may still run, or left an unresolved outside effect.

Observable postcondition

The cancelled-branch test neither waits for an impossible arrival nor asserts an unachieved result.

Known failure modes

  • Deadlock at an AND-join or false success after bypassing unfinished required work.

  • Adding cancellation introduces analysis complexity and residual-effect obligations.

Important criticisms
Adverse mechanism or cost

Adding cancellation introduces analysis complexity and residual-effect obligations.

Adjudication

Core coupling survives, but there is no universal rule that cancellation satisfies every join.

How the property evolved

REFINED: cancellation is treated as a state-changing operation with join consequences, not merely a visual exception arrow.

Mature or evolved form

When a branch is cancelled, update join obligations according to the declared scope and activation rather than pretending that cancellation produced a success token. Core coupling survives, but there is no universal rule that cancellation satisfies every join.

Ceremony vs property
Protected function

Deadlock at an AND-join or false success after bypassing unfinished required work.

Minimal adequate alternative

Cancel the enclosing unit and restart or adjudicate it as a whole when selective continuation is unnecessary.

Fuller form trigger

An interrupted branch can feed a later convergence point.

Consumer

Cancellation handler, join evaluator and responsible operator.

Cost of simplification

Removing the mechanism is acceptable only while the cheap path still establishes this claim: The cancelled-branch test neither waits for an impossible arrival nor asserts an unachieved result.

Retirement or omission

Retire or omit the extra machinery when the trigger, consumer or relevant dependency disappears, after settling/transferring the outstanding work or evidence that still relies on it. Cancel the enclosing unit and restart or adjudicate it as a whole when selective continuation is unnecessary.

Specify the scope ended by termination and account for live children, subscriptions, pending work items and transferred external obligations.

Classical workflow-net soundness combines option to complete, proper completion and absence of dead tasks.

Problem it addressed

An ordinary WF-net abstraction is being used for structural assurance. The consequential failure is Deadlock, leftover tokens or permanently dead tasks in the model.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Deadlock, leftover tokens or permanently dead tasks in the model.

Mechanism

Check the exact WF-net definition: every reachable marking has some path to the final marking, final completion leaves no residual tokens, and every transition can occur in some execution.

An ordinary WF-net abstraction is being used for structural assurance.

Non trigger or cheap path

For a trivial model, direct reachability reasoning or exhaustive small-state examination may suffice.

Dependencies or preconditions

A single source/sink WF-net and the relevant initial marking; a faithful abstraction of the property being claimed.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

Avoid or expose the controlled failure: One artificial case sequence obscures many-to-many dependencies or forces irrelevant tasks.

A mechanism-level rationale, not a measured universal benefit. Data patterns and data-centred models identify information/identity mechanisms. Field prevalence and economic effect of a particular binding policy remain poorly established by the inspected corpus.

Decision or consumer

Case worker and the coordinator of interacting business objects.

Actor and authority boundary

Object existence does not imply authority to modify its state.

Communication or interaction requirement

Communicate relevant object/state changes to affected task and case consumers.

Observable postcondition

A change in one object enables/constrains related work without losing its own identity or lifecycle obligations.

Known failure modes

  • One artificial case sequence obscures many-to-many dependencies or forces irrelevant tasks.

  • Cross-object interactions may enlarge the state space; wholesale case visibility can disclose excessive information.

Adjudication

Retain for fitting object structures; reject the claim that all workflows should be recast as one artefact model.

How the property evolved

ALTERNATIVE: data-centric forms complement rather than universally replace activity routing.

Mature or evolved form

Use available case data or interacting business-object states to determine permissible work when a single activity route would hide essential relationships. Retain for fitting object structures; reject the claim that all workflows should be recast as one artefact model.

Ceremony vs property
Protected function

One artificial case sequence obscures many-to-many dependencies or forces irrelevant tasks.

Minimal adequate alternative

An activity-centred process with explicit data bindings is preferable when it already represents the relationships clearly.

Fuller form trigger

Multiple related objects evolve asynchronously or work is naturally case/data-driven.

Consumer

Case worker and the coordinator of interacting business objects.

Cost of simplification

Removing the mechanism is acceptable only while the cheap path still establishes this claim: A change in one object enables/constrains related work without losing its own identity or lifecycle obligations.

Retirement or omission

Retire or omit the extra machinery when the trigger, consumer or relevant dependency disappears, after settling/transferring the outstanding work or evidence that still relies on it. An activity-centred process with explicit data bindings is preferable when it already represents the relationships clearly.

Concurrent data updates and isolated scopes affect the values used by routing and actions.

Problem it addressed

Data may change between enablement, claim and external action, or concurrent children update shared values. The consequential failure is An action is valid for an obsolete input but wrong for the current object.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

An action is valid for an obsolete input but wrong for the current object.

Mechanism

Choose binding/snapshot, conflict-detection or synchronisation rules sufficient for decisions that depend on mutable data; record when freshness cannot be established.

Trigger or context

Data may change between enablement, claim and external action, or concurrent children update shared values.

Non trigger or cheap path

Read-and-confirm immediately before a low-volume action or use immutable inputs instead of broad transactional machinery.

Dependencies or preconditions
Conditions

A relevance-specific freshness requirement and access to a version, timestamp or reliable source of current state.

Original form

Engine recovery state and external application state can diverge around a failure boundary.

Problem it addressed

An action may have committed outside the persisted workflow transition or a human acted outside the system. The consequential failure is Recovery repeats, omits or compensates an action based on an incorrect internal record.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Recovery repeats, omits or compensates an action based on an incorrect internal record.

Mechanism

Reconcile intent, recorded acknowledgement and authoritative external outcome before a recovery decision that would otherwise assume the world matches engine history.

Trigger or context

An action may have committed outside the persisted workflow transition or a human acted outside the system.

Non trigger or cheap path

An authoritative query or human confirmation may be more appropriate than a distributed transaction.

Dependencies or preconditions
Conditions

External action identity and a trustworthy observation or an explicit decision under unavoidable uncertainty.

Property application

Do not infer more than this observation; uncontrolled risk: External queries may be stale, unavailable or non-authoritative; reconciliation can become a costly second workflow.

Expected engineering payoff
Claim

Avoid or expose the controlled failure: Recovery repeats, omits or compensates an action based on an incorrect internal record.

Evidence qualification

A mechanism-level rationale, not a measured universal benefit. Durable/replay documentation and systems papers support implementation-specific guarantees. The strongest scoped result cannot be transferred to uncooperative external actions.

Decision or consumer

Recovery operator, external service owner and result consumer.

Actor and authority boundary

The reconciler may observe without being authorised to mutate; discrepancies require the right decision-maker.

Communication or interaction requirement

Exchange evidence of actual outcome, not merely duplicate copies of the original request.

Observable postcondition

The next recovery step states which external facts are established and which remain uncertain.

Known failure modes

  • Recovery repeats, omits or compensates an action based on an incorrect internal record.

  • External queries may be stale, unavailable or non-authoritative; reconciliation can become a costly second workflow.

Important criticisms
Adverse mechanism or cost

External queries may be stale, unavailable or non-authoritative; reconciliation can become a costly second workflow.

Adjudication

How the property evolved

REFINED: recovery continuity includes correspondence to external state, not only successful replay.

Mature or evolved form

Reconcile intent, recorded acknowledgement and authoritative external outcome before a recovery decision that would otherwise assume the world matches engine history. Retain conditional reconciliation rather than a requirement to query every pure task after every restart.

Ceremony vs property
Protected function

Recovery repeats, omits or compensates an action based on an incorrect internal record.

Minimal adequate alternative

An authoritative query or human confirmation may be more appropriate than a distributed transaction.

Fuller form trigger

An action may have committed outside the persisted workflow transition or a human acted outside the system.

Consumer

Recovery operator, external service owner and result consumer.

Cost of simplification

Removing the mechanism is acceptable only while the cheap path still establishes this claim: The next recovery step states which external facts are established and which remain uncertain.

Retirement or omission

Retire or omit the extra machinery when the trigger, consumer or relevant dependency disappears, after settling/transferring the outstanding work or evidence that still relies on it. An authoritative query or human confirmation may be more appropriate than a distributed transaction.

Original form

History-replay engines require deterministic orchestration relative to recorded events and commands.

Problem it addressed

The selected runtime rebuilds orchestration by replay. The consequential failure is Replay emits a different command sequence or repeats nondeterministic work as if it were pure control logic.

Failure mode it tries to prevent

Replay emits a different command sequence or repeats nondeterministic work as if it were pure control logic.

Mechanism

Keep replay-sensitive decisions within the deterministic contract and isolate or record nondeterministic inputs and effects through the supported interfaces.

Trigger or context

The selected runtime rebuilds orchestration by replay.

Non trigger or cheap path

A state-machine snapshot engine, explicit persisted state or a short transaction may not require this particular programming discipline.

Dependencies or preconditions
Conditions

The runtime’s command-matching rules, deterministic API constraints and separation of activities from orchestration.

Select a bounded subworkflow for the current case context and preserve the selection rationale and exception precedence when extending the rule base.
